howDoI.q: How do I make a map where one block is a whole town?
How do I give one scene its own, smaller picture of my hero?
How do I make a link that drops my hero on the cell I choose?
How do I make the way back land my hero where they came from?
How do I make a locked gate that needs a key from another scene?
How do I put a door in a house and land outside it on the way out?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Maps Within Maps is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short scenes: a world map, a town and a house, joined by links. A map file is only a grid of blocks, so a scene can draw a town as one block and the next scene can draw its streets house by house. It takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each idea is made.

Two other Starters teach other uses of links, so this one does not repeat them. Rooms on One Map puts several rooms on one map file, and The Same House reuses one map for different places. Overhead joins areas by their edges. Here every scene has a map of its own.

The keys

The four arrows walk Yana up, down, left and right. Space does nothing in this game. Walk onto the town, through a gate or in at a door to go on. Nothing in this game hurts Yana.

pages.head: Level 1: The World Map
pages.html:
Level 1: The World Map

Yana is tiny. They stand on a trail in a small country with the sea all round it, and the A TOWN IS ONE BLOCK sign says what the little ring of roofs is: the whole town, in one block. Walk onto it and the next scene opens.

A pair of keys lies in the east. Yana does not need them yet, but the town will send them back for them.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A block is whatever you draw it as. Every block is 20 by 20 pixels. In town.bbl the world's blocks are drawn from very far away: flat green land, sea, a few brown humps for hills and a few tiny pines for a forest. The town block is five small roofs and a flag. Nothing in Game-Maker says how big a block is in the world.
  • The shores are blocks too. There are sixteen land blocks, one for each way the sea can touch a square. The map uses the one with sand on its sea sides, so the coast is drawn without any code in the game.
  • Yana has a smaller picture here. The world scene loads tiny.chr and tiny.cbl instead of hero.chr and hero.cbl. They are the same walk drawn about half the size, set low in their block, so they look a tenth of the country across. The scene's file list in townlink.gam is where each scene picks its map, blocks and character.
  • The town block is a link. In the scene's links, the town block is the From and the cell inside the town's south gate is the To. Touching the block is all it takes.

pages.head: Level 2: The Town
pages.html:
Level 2: The Town

The same trip, much closer. Yana is full size, streets run between houses that are three blocks wide, and the town is bigger than the screen, so the view follows them. The YOU LAND AT THE GATE sign says they did not start at a corner of the town: the link put them two blocks inside its south gate.

The house at the top has a fence round its yard and a locked gate. Walk into the gate and it stops them; the sign says the keys are on the world map. The south gate takes them back out. Come back with the keys and the gate opens.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Its own map file. The town is town.map, 36 by 26 blocks, and the scene has scrolling on. The world is another file, world.map, so the two never share a cell. For several scenes that share one file, see Rooms on One Map.
  • The way back is its own link. A link goes one way. The town's south gate is two road blocks along the bottom edge, and each is the From of a link to the world scene. Its To is the trail block just below the town block, so they come out beside the town and not where the game began. If the To were the world's first cell, they would be back at the start of the trip.
  • A locked gate is a block. The gate has Solid sides checked, an Effect counter of the key counter and an Effect amount of minus one. With no key the counter would run out, so the touch is refused and the gate stays. With a key it is spent and the gate turns into road. The keys on the world map are the same counter with plus two: one for the gate on the way in, and one for the same gate on the way out of the yard, because the town map loads fresh each time they come back to it and the gate is shut again.
  • Counters travel with Yana. The key is picked up in one scene and spent in another, because a counter belongs to the hero and not to a scene. The first character file that loads sets the starting values, so the key counter starts at 1 in tiny.chr (a counter shows one less than it holds).
  • A door is a link. The door in the house's front is a block with a link on it. The wall blocks are solid; the door is not.

pages.head: Level 3: The House
pages.html:
Level 3: The House

Inside there is a rug, a table, a bed, shelves and three coins. The WALK OUT AND SEE WHERE YOU LAND sign asks you to try the door they came in by: it puts them in the yard just below the front door, not at the town gate or the corner. Go in again.

The door on the right wall under the EXIT sign is the way out of the game.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • A third scale. Furniture is one or two blocks: a bed is two blocks long, the table is two by two, and a plant is one. Yana is the same size as in the town, but next to a bed they are a person in a room, where next to a house they were a person in a street. Scale is what the other blocks are drawn as.
  • The door out lands in the yard. The door in the south wall is the From of a link to the town scene, and its To is the cell just below the house's front door. Every link names its own landing cell, so they can leave the same house by the same door and arrive in a different place each time you change that cell.
  • The far door ends the game. It is the From of a link to the game's last scene, the same as the exit door in the other Starters.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, from the original PLAYGAME code, so you can plan around them.

  • A link has no memory. A link always lands on the same To cell (StartSceneInits, PLAYGAME.C, lines 4642 to 4694). If two doors lead to the same scene, each needs its own link, and a door cannot send them back to whichever door they used. Here the town has one house door, so one way back is enough.
  • It cannot scale a picture. There is no zoom: every block is 20 by 20 pixels and the screen shows 16 by 10 of them. A small hero is a second set of small pictures, and a small town is a block drawn as a town.
  • It cannot change the hero's size inside a scene. A scene loads one character file, so a different size means a different scene.
  • Maps stay as they were. A coin picked up or a gate that turned into road is changed only for the visit: loading a scene loads its map again, so the gate is shut again when they come out of the house, and the world's keys are back on their block when they return to it. That is why the keys give two. The counters are the only thing they keep (StartSceneInits, PLAYGAME.C, lines 4655 to 4671).
  • It cannot make the counter show a number. The key counter is a number the game keeps, but nothing draws it as a digit on the screen.
  • It cannot land them on the top row or the left column of a screen that does not scroll. All three scenes here scroll, so the landing cells can be anywhere (chkscrnbounds, PLAYGAME.C, lines 3395 to 3435).

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In townlink.gam, open the town scene's links and change the To of the south gate to the world's first cell. Walk out and see where you land.
  • Open the world scene and give it hero.chr and hero.cbl in the file list. Yana is as big as the town's Yana and the world looks cramped.
  • In town.bbl, turn off Solid sides on the yard gate and the keys stop mattering.
  • Move the keys in world.map to the other end of the island.
  • Add a second house to town.map: give its door a link to a new scene of its own, with a map of its own.
  • In house.map, move the front door and its link, and set the town's To to the cell under it.

The home page’s Starters tab has more small games like this one.
